sections.h2: Two bills on one Memphis house
sections.html:
Your Memphis house sits in Shelby County, and city hall and the courthouse each tax it separately. County tax is figured and collected by the Trustee. The Treasury department of the city handles the city portion. Both rest on a value set by the Shelby County Assessor, and city tax on local property uses the assessment the Assessor certified as of January 1.

Two separate balances need to be paid off before you close. The city bill becomes payable after the City Council fixes the rate, usually in mid to late June, and it turns delinquent after August 31. The county bill follows the state calendar instead. Request a payoff from each office. A receipt from one never covers the other, and the title company needs both numbers.

Memphis is the Shelby County seat and Tennessee's second largest city. The 2020 census counted 633,104 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 609,647, a drop of 3.0% from that base. Shelby County as a whole has 910,226 people. The city has 253,120 households, and 44.9% of homes are owner-occupied, against 54.1% for the county. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $169,000, compared with $249,100 countywide, and median gross rent is $1,181.

With more than half of city households renting, many Memphis sellers are landlords. An investor selling a rental faces the same two bills as an owner who lives in the house, so the steps on this page apply to both.

sections.h2: When are Memphis and Shelby County property taxes due?
sections.html:
City and county bills follow separate clocks, which surprises a lot of sellers.

Memphis and Shelby County billing calendar
Bill detailCity of MemphisShelby County
Bill becomes payableAfter the Council sets the rate, usually mid to late JuneFirst Monday in October
Last day without penaltyAugust 31Last day of February
Interest once delinquent1.5% per month, 18% a yearAsk the Trustee for a payoff figure
Quarterly installments (age 65 and older)Aug 31, Nov 30, Feb 28, May 31Oct 31, Jan 31, Apr 30, Jul 31

The county offers no discount for paying early. It accepts partial payments, though interest keeps running on any balance left after the deadline.

City payments are taken at City Hall, 125 N. Main St., Suite 375, from 8:30 to 4:30. A check and the bill stub can go by mail to City of Memphis Treasury, P.O. Box 185, Memphis, TN 38101-0185. Phone payment is (901) 636-7200, the web portal is epayments.memphistn.gov, and any First Horizon Bank branch will accept the bill itself. A tax relief voucher cannot be used at the bank. For general questions, the Treasury information line is (901) 522-1111.

The county Trustee's office is at 157 Poplar Ave., with branch locations and a mailing address of P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751. Online and payit901 app payments are available. A $1.50 e-check fee or a 2.6% card fee applies, and the county keeps none of it.

The Trustee also runs ManagedPay, which spreads the current-year tax into monthly payments through February. Interest, legal fees and court action still attach to anything left unpaid after the deadline, so the plan fits an owner who is staying more than one about to close.

sections.h2: Tax relief and payment plans for older or disabled owners
sections.html:
Memphis owners can look at three programs, all governed by state eligibility rules.

  • Tax Relief: for owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled and receiving Social Security disability, who meet income limits, and for qualifying 100% disabled veteran owners and their surviving spouses.
  • Tax Freeze: for owners 65 or older whose income stays under the limit the state sets each year.
  • Quarterly Payment Program: for owners 65 or older who live in their primary residence and owe nothing delinquent.

The quarterly program needs a new application every year. Call the Trustee at (901) 222-0200 to ask when the next window opens and to confirm you qualify. Relief works as a reimbursement of tax already paid, so the bill itself is still yours to pay.

sections.h2: Can you dispute a Shelby County value?
sections.html:
Yes, though the season is short. Shelby County's equalization board hears appeals from May 1 through June 30, a month earlier than the June 1 opening most Tennessee counties use. Miss it and you wait for next spring.

The board sits at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Suite C-142, Memphis, TN 38134, and you can call (901) 222-7300. There is no filing fee. You can file online while the season is open, mail the form, or hand it in at the counter. Expect to carry the burden of proof, since the assessor's number starts out presumed right. Bring comparable sales, an outside appraisal, photographs of defects and repair quotes.

A neighbor's lower bill is not a reason the board will accept, and it cannot waive penalties, adjust rates or rule on exemptions. A written decision arrives roughly two weeks after the hearing. Anyone still unhappy has 45 days from that notice to take the case to the State Board of Equalization, which hears Memphis cases locally.

A successful appeal produces a refund of any overpayment, and the Treasury says refunds generally take about 60 days after it receives the change. Keep paying on schedule in the meantime.

sections.h2: Selling a Memphis house with taxes owed
sections.html:
Memphis can put weed cutting, demolition and board-up, sidewalk work and anti-neglect charges on the same bill. A house with a code history may owe a good deal beyond the tax. Downtown properties may also carry Central Business Improvement District taxes.

Once taxes are a full year late, the account goes to delinquent tax attorneys on February 1 and legal costs get added. Clear things up before that stage if you plan to list.

  1. Ask the City Treasury and the county Trustee each for a payoff figure good through your expected closing date.
  2. Check the record for city charges that ride on the bill, not only the tax.
  3. Hand both figures to the title company so it can pay each balance from your proceeds on closing day.
  4. Afterward, update the owner name. The Trustee bills the owner on the Assessor's rolls as of January 1 and also draws ownership data from deeds recorded with the Register, so call 901-222-0200 once the change is on record.
  5. If the mailing address on the city bill is wrong, send the Treasury a signed written request after the Assessor's office has processed the change.

A cash sale that closes as-is skips repair work and showing time, but the same two payoffs still come out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: When does Memphis city property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Once August 31 passes. Payment opens after the Council fixes the rate, typically around late June, and unpaid city balances then grow by 1.5% each month.

faqs.q: When is Shelby County property tax due?
faqs.a: Payment opens the first Monday of October and stays fee-free until February ends. Paying in October earns no discount.

faqs.q: Can I pay Memphis property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Owners 65 or older who live in the home and carry no delinquent balance can. The city splits the bill into four equal installments due August 31, November 30, February 28 and May 31. The Trustee sets its own terms, so ring (901) 222-0200.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Shelby County property value?
faqs.a: Send it to the county equalization board between May 1 and June 30. Nothing is charged to file, and (901) 222-7300 reaches staff who can help with the forms.

faqs.q: Does a Memphis house with unpaid tax have to be sold at auction?
faqs.a: Not by default. A real estate account a full year behind is handed to attorneys on February 1 with legal costs added, but settling it from your closing proceeds clears the debt before that point.
